instructions: Cut the 1.5 lbs ribeye into thin strips about 1/4 inch thick and 2 inches long, trimming off any thick fat. Pat them dry with paper towels and toss them with 3/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Make the awaze: in a small bowl, stir the 2 tbsp berbere, 1 tbsp of the olive oil, 2 tbsp water and the last 1/4 tsp salt into a loose paste.
Slice the red onion. Thinly slice the 4 garlic cloves. Cut the tomatoes into thin wedges and scoop out most of the seeds. Seed the jalapeño and slice it into strips.
Pull 2 sprigs off the rosemary and keep them whole. Cut the lemon in half.

Heat a large cast iron skillet over high until it's very hot, then add the last 2 tbsp olive oil. Add half the beef in a single layer and leave it for 1 minute, until the underside is browned. Stir and cook it for 1 minute, then move it to a plate. Brown the second half the same way. Stand back a little. It'll spatter.
Turn the heat to medium-high and add the onion. Cook it for 3 minutes, stirring, until it softens and the edges brown. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, jalapeño, rosemary sprigs, half the awaze and 2 tbsp water. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring and scraping up the brown bits, until the tomatoes just start to slump.
Put the beef back with any juices from the plate and toss it for about 1 minute, until it's coated and hot. It should still be a little pink in the middle.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the 2 tbsp ghee until it melts, and pull out the rosemary sprigs.
Taste it. If it's flat, add salt first, then a squeeze of lemon from one half.
Serve with injera or rice, with the rest of the awaze and the other lemon half cut into wedges on the side.
method_notes: All three cook bite-size beef fast in a hot pan with red onion, garlic, tomato, chili, berbere and rosemary, and finish with niter kibbeh or clarified butter. Gypsy Plate makes a separate awaze paste of berbere, oil and water, sears thin ribeye first, then adds onion, garlic, tomato, jalapeño and a rosemary sprig for a few minutes; this version keeps half the awaze for the table so the pan stays mild. Unpeeled Journal tosses ribeye with rosemary, ginger, garlic and a little berbere before it goes in and adds water at the end, while Cuisine Noir cooks it longer into a saucier, stew-like dish. No version had 20 or more ratings and the trusted cook for this cuisine (RecipeTin Eats) has no beef tibs, so this follows the top-rated version read.
